title: Project journal
how_written: One entry per project day, written from the dated Kean register (jobs/kean/register: findings, owner decisions, questions), the HANDOFF notes and the daily Mission checkpoints. Ready counts are the readiness tracker's 'ready for human review' on that day's last published generation; a day without a published generation shows none. Ready means a machine-complete dossier waiting for a person, not a certified result: certified whole lifecycles remain 0 throughout.
meaning: The project's question is the legally defensible life of every executive order from 1789 to the 14 October 2026 cutoff: when it began, what it commanded, whether and when each command ended, and what survives. In 25 days it went from no order ready for human review to 1,252 machine-complete dossiers, and from no settled status to a provisional yes or no for 4,274 orders.

Most of the value is not in the count but in the machinery that makes each next order cheaper and auditable: a census of 14,998 orders, a register of identities, held official printings for thousands of orders, a claim kit that turns research into checked claims, a checker that verifies every quotation against held bytes, a tracker that says exactly what each order still lacks, and Kean, which keeps every result and owner decision so no session starts from zero.

The count has fallen as well as risen, and that is the system working: on 7 November newly found official GPO printings made 193 earlier transcription-based dossiers stale, and they left the ready count until rechecked against the printing. Rules get stricter as evidence improves; nothing is counted on convenience.
What it does not mean yet: no lifecycle has been independently certified by a person. The 1,252 are ready for that review, with their remaining obligations stated.

summary: Ready rose from 1,083 (9 November) to 1,252 (10 November). Papinian contributed 63 canonical claims (PRs #257, #261), and the owner adopted six provisional NO statuses from its undecided probes. The Mabillon text-hash fix (Papebroch) and the P4 replica wiring also merged.

Ulpian: the owner declined a working-age floor, so adulthood counts only where an order's own text or another held source establishes it. The Jacquard L1 correction kept 9 of 42 statuses. Its L1R extension kept 70 of 556 and returns 486 to undecided (PR #289). The provisional-status count fell from 4,301 to 4,274 and falls further when #289 is reflected.

The overnight Codex wave spent about half the weekly Codex allowance and 97% of its input tokens were cache re-reads; it produced 12 claims on branches and none merged. The project already held the lessons, but nothing enforced them, so Augur now gates every wave: an outcome objective, Bentham actions only, a 1-lane 30-order first stage and a review by another model family or the owner.

Preparation for the next line: Accursius's F3-F7 claim-kit fixes (each reviewed by another model and fixed before approval), Respondendi's standing-approval design with two red-team rounds, Larrey's zero-token triage (0 of 130 past successes lost in back-test), Whitworth's registered cost forecast, and the owner's signatures on the Nalimov calibration and Codex smoke plans.

days.title: The rules of the road
days.story: The owner set the standing method: read the handoff at every session start, leave notes before stopping, run anything too large for an agent's machine as a bounded job on GitHub, and keep the immutable codebook. The first big plans all failed in instructive ways: an eight-job automation estimate, a sprint aiming for 300 ready orders, and 'family rules' that would let one shared text close a whole family. A library pilot compared PDF and citation tools on retained files.
milestones: First production sprint fails; lessons kept

days.title: The first 130
days.story: The first orders reached ready: a claim swarm on orders with exactly one named revoking order worked. The American Presidency Project was crawled through web-archive captures, which became the project's main independent transcription. HathiTrust GPO volumes for 1,712 orders could not be read that day, and a test of compact case packets did not beat ordinary preparation.

days.title: Sizing the mountain
days.story: An effort model put the remaining work at about 17,144 agent-hours, later 15,698. The X1 class engine began typing every pre-1937 order so whole classes could share rules. The owner was asked whether a lighter review could serve low-risk cases.

days.title: Modern orders and the first postmortem
days.story: Bowditch's modern status sweep worked; the modern claim factory did not. Lambertini recorded shared savings readings and counterevidence searches once for many orders. Llull wrote a postmortem of the project's first 23 plans, and Hamilton began auditing where tokens went.

days.title: Sixteen owner rulings
days.story: The owner decided sixteen legal and method questions in one day: how report deadlines on emergency boards end, that strike-and-insert amendments continue the order, that a statute not naming an order does not end it, how 'until' dates count, that AI-proposed statuses may be adopted only through review, and that transcriptions and ProQuest scans may serve as working texts. Ready doubled to 278.

days.title: The owner's ProQuest scans
days.story: Pinakes began ingesting the owner's ProQuest scans of the orders. Sinclair had a different AI family review 31 provisional NO proposals. The owner was asked for search keys (Brave, SerpAPI, NARA).

days.title: Labelled working texts
days.story: Provisional transcription support was labelled and restored verifications put back (PR #55), and one EO 12379 analysis was shared across six orders (PR #56).

days.title: Deterministic completion
days.story: kit.py complete replaced the agents that tallied and copied results, and earlier research now loads into each new case so work is never redone. The owner made ordinary production a standing protocol: prepare, view, apply, batch-check, complete.

days.title: Shared facts and record series
days.story: Norton tried answering a shared factual question once for several orders and stopped at its gate. The National Mediation Board's annual reports were read as an institutional record series.

days.title: Early Federal Register pages
days.story: The claim kit stopped picking neighbouring documents on crowded early Federal Register pages. Counterexample-first research did not beat ordinary research on six orders. Paired blind source reviews ran through the night.

days.title: Recovery after a reset
days.story: After a workspace reset, production batches and their whole-case attestations were recovered as explicit new versions rather than overwritten, and the human-checked citation gate learned to read qualified notes.

days.title: Evidence decides
days.story: The owner's central ruling: agents work out the legal distinctions themselves and record what the evidence establishes, with the best supported date or interval; a claim that something happened needs evidence that it did. Kean was born the same day, so every result and decision would be kept for the next session. The 1,530 one-person civil-service waivers were re-researched under the new ruling, and Namier began matching named people across every held text.

days.title: Coordinate by model tier
days.story: The owner ruled that the strongest model coordinates and keeps legal judgment while cheaper models take bounded tasks and scripts take deterministic work. Twenty-six findings in a day: production handoffs audited, hidden friction found, six wiring repairs made, Valla's context isolation repaired, and one independently reviewed shared legal analysis of the 1935 repeal of the NIRA code provisions.

days.title: Planted controls bound to the task
days.story: Planted-control reviews were bound to each lifecycle task's own scope, and shared NRA source research reconciled eight outliers. Ready approached 500.

days.title: Jacquard and Lachmann
days.story: Two engines arrived. Jacquard: the owner allowed sampled class review, with planted errors and zero misses allowed, to adopt provisional NO statuses for well-defined lots, and the waiver, NRA and Canal Zone lots were then reviewed member by member. Lachmann: machine collation that confirms a held working text is the right order, complete and on the right pages. The Apollo claim swarm worked 444 orders.

days.title: Erasmus
days.story: Erasmus resubmitted 40 Apollo rejects and corrected 20 flagged filed claims, and Geddes was wired into batch checking.

days.title: Recovered main, 784 ready
days.story: The combined recovered main generation was published and audited. Missing raw sources were retained through the queued route, Lachmann's checks were reused in ordinary preparation, and the production control center was packaged with the repository.

days.title: A lost run
days.story: The Bacon session's artifacts could not be recovered; the owner was asked for them, and the run was later closed as unrecoverable.

days.title: 1,331 ready
days.story: The biggest single-day rise. PRs 131-137 were integrated and the combined jobs run; source custody is now screened before any producer is dispatched; reviewed provision histories (MAITLAND) were carried into ordinary assignments. The owner delegated answers to eleven open questions, and the Mission rocket view was repaired to update itself.

days.title: Spend tokens where Bentham says
days.story: Bentham began ranking every possible action by measured yield per cost, and the owner made it the rule for every agent wave. Gessner cards gave each order one page. Tischendorf started proving official printings by comparing page text. Herschel took two probability samples of the 96,598 open order-steps. The owner bought Brave search credit and ruled that fee-based Archives reproductions are not needed.

days.title: The day of fifty-eight decisions
days.story: The largest day in the project's record: 95 findings, 58 owner decisions, 64 questions. The headline measure was fixed as operative force at the cutoff, the first-ending interval contract became claim schema v2, and a claim may now contest the ledger. Photius admitted official printings (R37) and microfilm witnesses (R38), and its lanes OCRed 9,086 pages of GPO volumes, read 2,557 ProQuest scans and page-checked free printings. Pothier wrote eleven family doctrines for 5,918 undecided orders, Mabillon proved 1,771 held government printings by text, and the repository's growth was paused near GitHub's cap. Ready peaked at 1,368.

days.title: Better evidence, honest drop
days.story: Ready fell from 1,185 to 992: Photius had found official GPO printings for 193 orders whose dossiers rested on transcriptions, so those confirmations went stale until checked against the printing. The response was evidence, not a script: Haloander rechecked against the printings and filed 25 lifecycle claims (992 to 1,017). Hansard serialized the progress refresh, and Ptolemy's and Selden's raw files moved to the release byte store.

days.title: Cujas and Montfaucon
days.story: The owner said yes to all four Haloander questions. Cujas page-checked 68 Photius-stale orders against their GPO printings with two blind arms and planted controls, all six controls caught. Montfaucon's paired blind readers produced 500 original-page outcomes, including honest negatives where agency reports were reprints, not issued originals. One dashboard replaced several (Tsiolkovsky folded in), and Riquet split long job chains into segments.

days.title: Papebroch and the rerun rule
days.story: Papebroch closed the Mabillon text-hash hole held since 6 November: 2,015 government-printed passages now verify, Lachmann reads them, and working-text confirmations rise from 715 to 776 with none lost (PR #244, measured, awaiting merge). The owner ruled that the claim checker must rerun only the claims a change can reach, after a 50-minute full run was spent on a change touching one claim, and that Lachmann runs after Mabillon. The Gutenberg wave made costs honest and added a read audit and daily chain health (PR #242).

days.title: Papinian, Ulpian and the Augur gate
days.story: Papinian filed and merged 63 canonical claims (PRs #257 and #261), and the owner adopted six provisional NO statuses it proposed; ready ended the day at 1,252. The owner declined any flat working-age floor (Ulpian), so the Jacquard statuses that rested on 'anyone employed by 1917 was at least 14' were read again: 9 of 42 wave-1 rows kept and, in the follow-up, 70 of 556 kept and 486 returned to undecided (PR #289), each by two blind arms that caught every planted control. The overnight Codex wave spent about half the weekly Codex allowance for 12 claims and none merged, with 83% of its reserved orders outside any Bentham action; Augur now refuses a wave without an outcome objective, Bentham actions, a measured ramp and an outside review. Accursius's five claim-kit fixes, Respondendi's standing-approval design, Larrey's zero-token triage and the signed Nalimov calibration plan prepare the next production line.
